--- title: "[Graph.get_edge_df()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get edges as a Polars DataFrame with standardized structure. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L7776-L7900){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_edge_df() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns all edges with a consistent column structure: - column 1: `id` (i64, mandatory, sorted ascending) - column 2: `source` (i64, mandatory) - column 3: `target` (i64, mandatory) - column 4: `rel` (str, mandatory, null if not set) - columns 5-N: Other attributes (alphabetically sorted) - weight is included as a special attribute if present The DataFrame is always sorted by edge ID in ascending order. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pl.DataFrame]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A Polars DataFrame with edges sorted by `id`. Returns an empty DataFrame if the graph has no edges. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The layout mirrors `get_node_df()` in spirit: `id`, `source`, `target`, and `rel` always come first (in that order), followed by `weight` and any other custom edge attributes in alphabetical order, with rows sorted by `id` ascending. `weight` is treated as a first-class attribute column rather than a bare number so it can be filtered and aggregated with the rest of the schema. Missing `rel` values appear as `None`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Every edge DataFrame starts with `id`, `source`, `target`, and `rel`, followed by `weight` and any other custom attributes: ::: {#f91a8010 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node("A") .add_node("B") .add_node("C") .add_node("D") .add_edge("A", "B", weight=1.5, rel="friend") .add_edge("B", "C", weight=2.0, rel="colleague") .add_edge("C", "D", weight=1.0, rel="friend") ) df = graph.get_edge_df() df.columns ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['id', 'source', 'target', 'rel', 'weight'] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#0834fcce .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df.shape ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (3, 5) ``` ::: ::: Being a regular Polars DataFrame, it supports the usual filtering and aggregation -- for example, isolating edges of a given relationship type: ::: {#a6e8f5a0 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl df.filter(pl.col("rel") == "friend") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

334"friend"1.0
``` ::: ::: Or grouping to count how many edges fall into each relationship type: ::: {#20a3e182 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} df.group_by("rel").count() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` /var/folders/s8/bj_jsx3d7jqd2btw7bwm6yx80000gp/T/ipykernel_6156/3133314846.py:1: DeprecationWarning: `GroupBy.count` was renamed; use `GroupBy.len` instead df.group_by("rel").count() ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Aggregating `weight` per group works the same way as with any Polars DataFrame: ::: {#a80bde34 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} df.group_by("rel").agg(pl.col("weight").mean()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
